body_markdown:
The Nissan Pathfinder turns 40 years old in 2026. Nissan is celebrating this milestone by releasing a Special Edition variant of[the current, fifth-generation model](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2023-nissan-pathfinder-rock-creek-review-mojo-returns/) that gains some retro flair, including throwback exterior emblems and a two-tone interior.


Riding on black-finished 20-inch alloy wheels, the Pathfinder Special Edition stands out with red accents on the grille, an edition-specific emblem on each C-pillar, and big “PATHFINDER” lettering on the hatch. The look is fairly subtle until you step inside, where you’ll find two-tone black and red upholstery inspired by the red cloth interior that was available on the original Pathfinder.


Nissan is throwing in a generous selection of standard features, including a panoramic moonroof, second-row captain’s chairs, rear sunshades, and a 12-speaker Bose sound system. There are no mechanical changes to report, however, so power comes from a 3.5-liter V-6 rated at 284 horsepower and 259 pound-feet of torque. Front-wheel-drive and a nine-speed automatic transmission come standard, and all-wheel drive is offered as an extra cost. The standard hitch receiver lets the Pathfinder tow up to 6000 pounds.

Built in Tennessee, the 2027 Nissan Pathfinder Special Edition will go on sale nationwide in November 2026. Pricing starts at $48,965 for the front-wheel-drive Special Edition, while adding all-wheel drive bumps the price up to $50,965. Note that both figures include a $1575 destination charge. For context, the base 2027 Pathfinder starts at $41,565 including destination.


This isn’t the first time Nissan has drawn inspiration from the 1980s to launch a limited-edition model. In 2023, the Japanese brand released[the Frontier Hardbody Edition](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/nissan-brings-back-the-hardbody-truck-with-a-tribute-model/) with several throwback styling cues, such as 17-inch wheels and a bed-mounted sport bar.
